answer: Peers only attest participants whose reputation climbs toward a verified summit of sustained honest work, while low-stake newcomers like a lone sparrow stay throttled until they earn trust. Each agent must stake tokens and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to its graph vertex, so forging identities costs real compute and capital. Duplicating identities thus multiplies cost without multiplying reward, making sybil swarms economically irrational. In practice, Agent0011 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
